head: e9121976

findings.title: SQL Server bracket escaping does not double an embedded `]` for declared PIVOT value identifiers

source.detail: the typed Pivot overload turns the projection-declared value strings into PivotValue.Create(declared[i]) and formats the member alias via dialect.Escape(name)

sinks.detail: public override string Escape(string keyword) => "[" + keyword + "]"; - wraps the identifier without doubling an embedded `]` (contrast QuoteIdentifier at :171 which does name.Replace("]", "]]"))
SqlServerPivotRenderer.RenderPivot: sb.Append(dialect.Escape(pivot.Values[i].Value)); - the declared value reaches Escape in the IN (...) list

findings.payload_effect: a declared value `1], [2` renders `[1], [2]` - two identifiers instead of one escaped identifier

findings.title: Raw UNPIVOT role names / SqlFunctions.Column<T> names rendered unquoted

source.detail: the typed Unpivot extracts the role identifiers (PivotProjectionRewriter.ExtractUnpivotRoles) and builds the typed source with an identity formatValueName (`static name => name`), so the runtime role strings are not escaped

sinks.detail: AppendIdentifier appends the name raw when _options.QuoteIdentifiers is false, else _dialect.QuoteIdentifier(name); the captured runtime role/value identifier flows into the rendered projection

findings.payload_effect: a captured role such as `0+(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sys.tables)` becomes an executable projection expression instead of a quoted identifier

issue.title: Identifier safety: SQL Server bracket escaping and raw UNPIVOT/Column<T> names
